description: v1 anchor: raw-feature 5-fold LightGBM, no FE
notes: PURPOSE: anchor run, not a competitive attempt. Establishes the first (OOF, LB) pair so the OOF<->LB relationship can eventually be measured (playbook s4) and a gate set. HYPOTHESIS: none - this is the measuring instrument, not a probe. SETUP: 12 raw features, no FE, LightGBM near-default (lr 0.05, num_leaves 31, n_estimators cap 8000, early stop 100), frozen StratifiedKFold(5, shuffle=True, random_state=42), categoricals as pandas category with a train-union-test vocab (unsupervised label mapping, not a leak). LOCAL RESULT: OOF AUC 0.963320, folds [0.962584, 0.963192, 0.963605, 0.964183, 0.963065], spread 0.0016, best_iters [3000, 2128, 2145, 2317, 2255] (cap 8000 does not bind - verified by assert). EDA FINDINGS: (1) missingness is uninformative - every missing-indicator scores AUC ~0.500, so indicator features are noise and the train/test null-rate gaps are not drift; (2) no train/test distribution drift on any column (max KS 0.0; max Cramers V 0.0); (3) marginal signal is concentrated in screen-time (daily_screen_time 0.890, weekend_screen_time 0.881, social_media 0.858) BUT split-count importance ranks notifications_per_day 1st and app_opens_per_day 2nd despite marginal AUCs of 0.492 and 0.541 - rank gaps +8 and +4. Those two are interaction-only; marginal-signal feature selection would have dropped exactly what the model leans on hardest. NEXT PROBE (highest prior): explicit interaction terms notifications/app_opens, app_opens/daily_screen_time, notifications/daily_screen_time. CAVEAT: early stopping picks the tree count on the fold it then scores, so OOF is slightly optimistic - constant across runs, so comparisons are unaffected.

description: A1 seed twin: model_seed 42->43, nothing else
notes: PURPOSE: measure the OOF noise floor to set a PROVISIONAL gate. HYPOTHESIS: none - this is an instrument, not a probe. TEST: strict twin of champion ba6c676a, only LightGBM random_state changes (42->43); the CV partition is untouched so the OOF rows are identical. GATE: n/a. INTERPRETATION: whatever |delta OOF| appears here is how much OOF moves when NOTHING meaningful changed, so any future delta below it is noise. Provisional gate = max(this delta, 3x paired-bootstrap SE from compare_oof.py). This is a FLOOR only - it captures estimation noise but not OOF->LB transfer noise, so it will be too permissive rather than too strict, and gets replaced by the section-4 residual sigma once ~10 paired runs exist.

description: B1: interaction ratios (opens_per_hour, notif_per_hour, notif_per_open)
notes: HYPOTHESIS: notifications_per_day and app_opens_per_day rank 9th/6th of 12 on marginal AUC (0.492/0.541) but 1st/2nd on split usage. A GBDT cannot express x/y with axis-aligned splits, so it is burning capacity approximating these ratios; supplying them explicitly should free that capacity. MECHANISM PREDICTED: split usage should shift OFF the raw notifications/app_opens columns and ONTO the new ratios, and OOF should rise. PRE-SCREEN (read-only, no training): notif_per_hour solo AUC 0.2639 (lift 0.236, inverted) vs 0.492 for the raw column; opens_per_hour 0.3024 (lift 0.198) vs 0.541. GATE (pre-registered BEFORE seeing the result): +0.0002 OOF, = 3x the measured seed-twin delta of 0.000066 from run 22de9888; 3x paired-bootstrap SE is 0.000089, so 0.0002 is the conservative choice. PROVISIONAL - replaced by the section-4 residual sigma once ~10 paired runs exist. TEST: strict twin of champion ba6c676a, only fe_interaction flips False->True. WATCH: a ratio is NaN if either operand is missing, so these cover ~78% of rows vs ~90% for the raw columns; if the probe underperforms its solo AUC, check coverage before concluding the family is dead.

description: A2a: champion with early_stop 100->400
notes: PURPOSE: isolate an early-stopping confound found in B1, not a feature probe. FINDING THAT PROMPTED IT: B1's entire loss (-0.000273) came from fold 0, whose best_iter collapsed 3000->1055 while folds 2/3/4 were flat within noise; fold AUC std rose 0.000538->0.000884. On a plateau this flat, patience=100 lets a fold quit while still improving, injecting per-fold noise of order 0.001 - which SWAMPS the +0.0002 gate and would corrupt every probe in B2-B5 identically. HYPOTHESIS: patience 400 stabilises best_iter selection and shrinks fold-AUC std. TEST: strict twin of champion ba6c676a, only early_stop changes. GATE: this is a harness measurement, not a shipping decision - judged on fold_auc_std and on whether fold 0's best_iter stops collapsing, not on OOF alone.

description: B6: per-value target encoding of all 9 numeric columns (nested, fold-safe)
notes: HYPOTHESIS: value->target is NON-MONOTONE, so no unsupervised transform can capture it but a supervised per-value lookup can. MECHANISM: notifications_per_day values carry positive rates spanning 0.119..0.986 while Pearson(value,rate)=-0.044 and only 47.8pct of steps increase - AUC sees only monotone association (raw 0.492), a tree CAN carve individual values (hence its top split-usage rank), a ratio CANNOT (hence B1's failure). This is KAGGLE_PLAYBOOK.md section 6: no unsupervised binning recreates a value->label mapping; B1 was exactly that forbidden imitation. GATE: +0.0002 vs A2a (6b671f87, OOF 0.963405). RESULT: OOF 0.966384, +0.002979 = ~15x gate, ~45x seed noise. LEAK AUDIT: train/val encoding-AUC gaps -0.0012..+0.0025 (singleton columns NEGATIVE, opposite of leakage); fold std FELL 0.000555->0.000413 and spread 0.001656->0.001130 (a leak inflates both); best_iter fell 3000-3998 -> 1161-2614, i.e. the model converges faster given information it previously built split-by-split - the predicted mechanism. PRE-REGISTERED FALSIFICATION: calibration (n=4, Spearman +1.000, residual sigma 0.000064) predicts LB = OOF + 0.001719 = 0.96810 +/- 0.0002. An LB materially below that means the OOF is inflated and the encoder leaks despite the audit. Recorded BEFORE submitting.

description: B7: add target-encoded cross notifications_per_day x app_opens_per_day
notes: HYPOTHESIS: if the single-column value->target relation is a lookup table (confirmed in B6), the PAIRWISE relation may be too. A cross is the only encoding expressing 'this COMBINATION of values' rather than 'this value of x'. Supervised form of what B1 attempted with ratios and failed at. TEST: strict twin of B6 (f64e2781, OOF 0.966384), only te_crosses differs. GATE: +0.0002 OOF vs B6; same family so the 0.0002 TE-family offset does not apply. RISK: cardinality - up to 38k cells over 691k rows (~18/cell) vs ~2700 rows/value for single columns, so per-row self-influence rises ~0.03pct -> ~3pct. Nesting and smoothing become load-bearing, and the train/val gap audit (which had NO power on single columns: a deliberately leaky fit scored only +0.0008) becomes a genuine test. DISQUALIFIER: gap > +0.02 on the cross column means leak, regardless of OOF. PREDICTED LB if it clears: OOF + 0.001496 (TE-family offset), NOT + 0.001719.

description: B8: capacity - num_leaves 31->255, min_child_samples 20->50
te_cols: age daily_screen_time_hours social_media_hours gaming_hours work_study_hours sleep_hours notifications_per_day app_opens_per_day weekend_screen_time
notes: HYPOTHESIS: num_leaves=31 is the LightGBM default and is under-capacity for 691k rows; the target-encoded model already converges in ~1100-2600 trees (down from 3000-4000 pre-TE), which suggests it is depth-limited rather than iteration-limited. min_child_samples raised 20->50 alongside to keep leaves populated at higher capacity - NOTE this makes it a 2-parameter change within the single lgb_params field, so it is a capacity-BUNDLE probe, not a clean one-parameter twin; if it clears, a follow-up must separate the two. TEST: twin of B6 (f64e2781, OOF 0.966384). GATE: +0.0002 OOF. WATCH: overfitting shows as best_iter collapsing while OOF falls; if fold std rises sharply, capacity is too high.

description: B10: XGBoost screening run on the B6 target-encoded feature set
te_cols: age daily_screen_time_hours social_media_hours gaming_hours work_study_hours sleep_hours notifications_per_day app_opens_per_day weekend_screen_time
notes: PURPOSE: section 5 ensemble axis - is there a second STRONG and DECORRELATED learner? NOT a strict twin (different learner; lr 0.10 x 1500 rounds chosen to approximate lr 0.05 x 3000 total shrinkage within the local 10-min budget), so its solo OOF is NOT comparable to B6's at gate resolution. The comparable question is disagreement vs B6 on identical OOF rows, and whether a fixed-ratio blend beats B6 on OOF. Section 6: high disagreement WITHOUT competitive solo strength is noise wearing a costume. Not submitted - screening offline now that calibration licenses it.

description: blend f64e2781+7ebde432 weights [0.5, 0.5]
notes: Section 5 blend: B6 LightGBM + B10 XGBoost, both on the target-encoded feature set, fixed round weights chosen by NESTED CV (ratio picked on 4 folds, scored on the held-out 5th) so the justifying number is not the number the weight was fitted on. Nested CV chose 1:1 in 4 of 5 folds; held-out gain over the best solo +0.000263, clearing the +0.0002 gate. Disagreement between the two legs is 1.931pct against a 1.450pct seed-noise floor (run 22de9888), so the diversity is modest but real and comes WITH competitive solo strength - not section 6's 'noise wearing a costume'. Rank-averaging scored 0.966911 vs probability-averaging 0.966902, indistinguishable, so the simpler probability average is used. Deliberately NOT hill-climbed: section 5 records that a simplex search over 51 models bought +0.00014 (~0.5 sigma of pure selection bias) and once collapsed to weight 1.0 on a single model.

description: C1: learning_rate 0.05->0.02 on the B6 target-encoded feature set (Kaggle kernel)
te_cols: age daily_screen_time_hours social_media_hours gaming_hours work_study_hours sleep_hours notifications_per_day app_opens_per_day weekend_screen_time
notes: HYPOTHESIS: smaller step size with proportionally more trees finds a finer optimum; standard GBDT behaviour, typically worth +0.0005..0.001. Motivated by B8, which showed the model is NOT depth-limited (num_leaves 255 collapsed best_iter to ~300 and LOST 0.000249), pointing at step size rather than capacity as the remaining optimisation lever. WHY ON KAGGLE: lr 0.02 needs ~2.5x the trees and exceeded the ~10-min local budget twice; Kaggle allows 9h. TEST: strict twin of B6 (f64e2781, OOF 0.966384) - only learning_rate differs. GATE: +0.0002 OOF vs B6, same family so no offset adjustment. WATCH: best_iter should reach ~4000-6500; hitting the 8000 cap means under-trained, not converged. IF IT CLEARS: the champion is the 1:1 BLEND (b171c0cf), not B6 alone, so the blend must be rebuilt on this leg with the ratio re-derived by nested CV - a stronger leg that is also more correlated with the XGBoost leg can leave the blend flat or worse.

description: blend 6a091632+7ebde432 weights [0.5, 0.5]
notes: NOT SUBMITTED - did not clear the gate. C1 (lr 0.02) + XGB nested-CV held-out 0.966969 vs the CURRENT CHAMPION blend B6+XGB at 0.966897: delta +0.000073, well under the pre-registered +0.0002. A 3-way B6+C1+XGB was +0.000071, also under. MECHANISM (playbook section 6, strength vs decorrelation, now measured on our own models): C1 beat B6 as a solo leg (+0.000220, which DID clear the gate) but disagrees with the XGBoost leg on only 1.843pct of rows versus B6's 1.931pct against a 1.450pct seed-noise floor. The stronger leg is also the more correlated one, so most of its solo gain is cancelled by the diversity it costs. This is why a leg that clears the gate does not automatically make a better SUBMISSION when the champion is a blend. Artifacts archived so this is retro-blendable if the gate or the leg set changes later.

description: C2: target-encoding inner folds 5->20
te_cols: age daily_screen_time_hours social_media_hours gaming_hours work_study_hours sleep_hours notifications_per_day app_opens_per_day weekend_screen_time
notes: HYPOTHESIS: a structural mismatch inside the winning lever. Training rows get their encoding from an inner-OOF fit on 80% of the training fold; val and test rows get theirs from a fit on 100% of it. The model therefore learns against a noisier, differently-distributed version of the feature than it is scored on. Raising the inner folds 5->20 shrinks the fitting set gap from 80% to 95% and cuts the variance of the training-row encodings, without weakening the nesting at all (a row still never sees its own label). MECHANISM PREDICTION: if this is real, best_iter should RISE (a cleaner feature supports more trees before overfitting). GATE: +0.0002 OOF over B6 0.966384. Cost is 4x the encoding work, which is bincount-cheap next to the tree fitting.

description: C3: XGBoost max_depth 6->8 on the B6 target-encoded feature set
te_cols: age daily_screen_time_hours social_media_hours gaming_hours work_study_hours sleep_hours notifications_per_day app_opens_per_day weekend_screen_time
notes: HYPOTHESIS: the blend screen showed XGBoost is load-bearing -- every blend containing B10x beats every blend without it, and B10x is also the strongest solo leg (0.966632) -- yet it is the ONLY leg never tuned, still at the depth-6 screening default while the LightGBM side has had lr, leaves and TE probes. depth 6 = 64 leaves is plausibly under-capacity for 691k rows with 9 target-encoded columns, and B10x stopped early (872-948 iters) which is consistent with capacity, not overfitting, being the binding constraint. MECHANISM PREDICTION: best_iter should FALL (more capacity per tree = fewer trees). RISK per section 6: a stronger XGB leg may also be a more correlated one, exactly as C1 was on the LightGBM side -- so measure disagreement vs B6, do not assume. GATE: +0.0002 solo OOF over B10x 0.966632 to count as a better leg; shipping still requires the re-derived blend to clear +0.0002 over champion 0.966895.

description: D1: CatBoost third leg on the B6 target-encoded feature set (Kaggle kernel)
te_cols: age daily_screen_time_hours social_media_hours gaming_hours work_study_hours sleep_hours notifications_per_day app_opens_per_day weekend_screen_time
notes: HYPOTHESIS: the ensemble axis needs a different FAMILY, not a better LightGBM. Offline screening of all 10 pairs and 10 triples over the 5 existing legs found NOTHING clearing +0.0002 over champion 0.966895 (best B7+B10x+C1 at +0.000127); the two LightGBM configs B6/C1 disagree on only 0.975% of rows, BELOW the 1.450% seed-noise floor, i.e. they are near-substitutes. CatBoost differs structurally: symmetric oblivious trees + ordered boosting. MECHANISM PREDICTION: disagreement vs B10x XGBoost ABOVE 1.931%. If below, a family change bought nothing and the ensemble axis is closed. SCREEN: solo OOF within 0.001 of B6 0.966384. GATE (shipping): re-derived blend must clear +0.0002 nested-CV held-out over champion 0.966895.

SHIP: champion blend + the CatBoost family. D1 is the first leg to break the section-6 strength/decorrelation tradeoff -- strongest solo (0.966890, above the whole champion BLEND at 0.966902) AND most decorrelated (2.063% vs XGB, above the 1.931% threshold pre-registered before the run). Chosen by a STATED RULE, not by maximum: add the new family to the existing champion, one leg per family, equal weights. All 25 CatBoost-containing blends cleared +0.0002 spanning +0.00027..+0.00038, so picking the argmax would have been the section-5 selection bias -- the spread is noise. Equal weights fit NOTHING. Nested-CV held-out +0.000333; equal-weight full OOF +0.000295 with all 5 folds positive (+0.000276..+0.000331). Predicted LB 0.96882 from offset +0.001620 +/- 0.000143.

description: D2: declare the 9 numeric columns categorical (LightGBM screen)
te_cols: age daily_screen_time_hours social_media_hours gaming_hours work_study_hours sleep_hours notifications_per_day app_opens_per_day weekend_screen_time
notes: HYPOTHESIS: acts directly on the central EDA finding. notifications_per_day carries per-value positive rates spanning 0.119..0.986 while Pearson(value, rate) = -0.044 and only 47.8% of consecutive steps increase -- a LOOKUP TABLE, not a function. That is why its solo AUC is 0.492 yet it ranks 1st on split usage, and why B1's ratio feature failed (a ratio is a monotone transform and cannot represent a lookup). If the values are labels rather than magnitudes then ordered axis-aligned splits are the wrong tool and a categorical many-vs-many split is the right one. This is the UNSUPERVISED lever for the structure that the supervised lever (B6 target encoding) already exploited for +0.003 -- so the honest prior is that TE has already extracted most of it and this is largely redundant. MECHANISM PREDICTION: if it is redundant, the __te columns keep their split share and the score barely moves; if it is complementary, split usage shifts toward the raw categorical columns. GATE: +0.0002 OOF over B6 0.966384. This is a CHEAP LightGBM screen for whether the far more expensive CatBoost version (2.2h/kernel, ordered target statistics) is worth a cycle.

description: D2b: categorical ONLY for the two lookup-table columns
te_cols: age daily_screen_time_hours social_media_hours gaming_hours work_study_hours sleep_hours notifications_per_day app_opens_per_day weekend_screen_time
notes: HYPOTHESIS: D2 was right about the structure and wrong about the scope. Declaring all nine numerics categorical cost -0.004041 and collapsed best_iter 1860->450, because seven of them are strongly MONOTONE -- daily_screen_time_hours 0.8896 solo AUC over 1389 levels, weekend_screen_time 0.8810 over 1437 -- so categorifying them discards genuine ordinal signal AND creates a 1400-level feature LightGBM overfits. The lookup-table property belongs only to notifications_per_day (solo 0.4921, 231 levels) and app_opens_per_day (0.5409, 166 levels), which are exactly the two columns that rank 1st and 2nd on split usage despite near-chance marginal AUC. Restrict the treatment to those two. MECHANISM PREDICTION: best_iter should return to the ~1800 range, since the overfitting driver was the 1400-level screen-time columns and not the 166/231-level ones. GATE: +0.0002 OOF over B6 0.966384. HONEST PRIOR: still low, because B6 target encoding is the SUPERVISED lever on this same structure and already took +0.003 out of it.

description: E1: PyTorch MLP -- a fourth model family on the B6 target-encoded feature set
te_cols: age daily_screen_time_hours social_media_hours gaming_hours work_study_hours sleep_hours notifications_per_day app_opens_per_day weekend_screen_time
notes: HYPOTHESIS: the probe record says families win and knobs do not. Since target encoding, EVERY within-family tuning probe missed the gate -- C1's blend +0.000073, C2 +0.000062, C3 +0.000001, D2 -0.004041, D2b -0.001835 -- and the single win was adding a family (D1 CatBoost, which shipped the champion from 0.96831 to 0.96847). A neural net shares no inductive bias with a gradient-boosted tree at all: it fits smooth global functions instead of axis-aligned partitions, so it should be the most decorrelated leg available. MECHANISM PREDICTION: disagreement vs the tree legs ABOVE D1 CatBoost's 2.063%, which is the current record. Solo OOF is EXPECTED TO BE LOWER than the trees -- trees dominate tabular data and the target encoding was built for them -- so this leg is judged on the blend, not on solo. NOTE this is the first model in the notebook that needs scaling and imputation, both fit on the training fold only, same rule as the target encoder. GATE (shipping): re-derived blend must clear +0.0002 nested-CV held-out over champion 0.967197.

SHIP: add a FOURTH family. E1 MLP is by far the most decorrelated leg measured -- 2.827-3.165% disagreement vs the tree legs against D1 CatBoost's previous record of 2.063% and a 1.450% seed floor -- and it achieves that while being the WEAKEST leg solo (0.965935, below every tree). Pre-registered prediction was exactly this: above 2.063% disagreement, solo below the trees, judged on the blend not on solo. Same stated rule as D1: add the new family to the existing champion, one leg per family, equal weights, which fit nothing. +0.000254 equal-weight full OOF, positive on all 5 folds (+0.000197..+0.000307); nested-CV held-out +0.000223. NOT the argmax -- B10x+D1cat+E1mlp scored +0.000252 nested by dropping B6, and taking it would be the section-5 selection bias. Predicted LB 0.96879 using the blend offset ~+0.00134, which is itself the unproven n=2 hypothesis, so treat the prediction loosely.

description: E2: MLP with learned embeddings for the two lookup-table columns
te_cols: age daily_screen_time_hours social_media_hours gaming_hours work_study_hours sleep_hours notifications_per_day app_opens_per_day weekend_screen_time
notes: HYPOTHESIS: the REGULARISED version of D2, which failed. D2/D2b showed a tree SPLIT on a 166/231-level lookup column overfits -- best_iter collapsed 1860->503 and OOF fell 0.0018 to 0.0040. An embedding is the same per-value lookup fitted by gradient descent under weight decay, so the capacity is penalised rather than unconstrained, and the EDA's non-monotone value->rate map (0.119..0.986, Pearson -0.044) is exactly what an embedding table represents and an axis-aligned split cannot. MECHANISM PREDICTION: disagreement vs the tree legs should RISE above E1's 2.827-3.165%, because the embedding gives the net a representation no tree leg has. GATE: shipping requires the re-derived blend to clear +0.0002 nested-CV held-out over champion 0.967451. Solo is NOT the criterion -- E1 shipped as the weakest leg on the board.

description: C4: XGBoost with the 30-trial Optuna config, validated on the frozen 5-fold
te_cols: age daily_screen_time_hours social_media_hours gaming_hours work_study_hours sleep_hours notifications_per_day app_opens_per_day weekend_screen_time
notes: HYPOTHESIS: plan section C -- tuning only after the feature set is settled, which it now is (every FE family probe missed; target encoding is the one feature lever that paid). XGBoost chosen because the offline blend screen showed it is load-bearing (every blend containing it beat every blend without it) and it is the least-tuned leg. 30 GPU trials, 250k stratified subsample, 3-fold, roc_auc objective, target encoder re-fit inside every fold of every trial per section 2. SEARCH RESULT ALREADY WEAK: span 0.963503..0.964603 and the best is only +0.000184 over trial 0, and it returned max_depth=6 -- our existing default -- independently reproducing C3's finding that depth is not the lever. HONEST CAVEAT: the search subsample overlaps the frozen OOF rows, so the search score is optimistic; THIS run on the frozen 5-fold is the only number that counts. GATE: +0.0002 solo OOF over B10x 0.966632, and shipping still needs the re-derived blend to clear +0.0002 over champion 0.967451.

description: E3: MLP on RAW features -- no target encoding
notes: HYPOTHESIS: every one of the 11 legs so far uses the identical B6 target-encoded feature set, so feature representation has been held CONSTANT across the entire model portfolio and the section 6 wall test was measured over architecture variation only. Target encoding hands the model a supervised summary of each value; without it the net must learn the value->rate map from the raw column itself, which is a different function class and a different failure mode. MECHANISM PREDICTION: solo OOF will FALL noticeably (TE was worth +0.003 to the trees) but disagreement should rise above E2's 3.352% record, because the leg now differs from the others in INPUT as well as architecture. GATE: shipping requires the re-derived blend to clear +0.0002 over champion 0.967451. This probe exists to test whether the wall I claimed is a property of the data or an artefact of having varied only one thing.

description: F1: RealMLP (pytabkit) -- a fifth family, not another MLP shape
te_cols: age daily_screen_time_hours social_media_hours gaming_hours work_study_hours sleep_hours notifications_per_day app_opens_per_day weekend_screen_time
notes: HYPOTHESIS: I claimed the ensemble axis was closing from Spearman -0.645 over 11 legs, but those legs were 3 tree libraries plus ONE MLP shape, all on the SAME target-encoded feature set -- a narrow space to declare a wall over. RealMLP brings periodic-linear (PLR) numeric embeddings, its own scaling pipeline and LR schedule, and is the strongest published tabular-NN baseline. Validation split passed explicitly so it never sees val labels via an internal random split; NaNs imputed with the TRAINING FOLD median with missing indicators retained. MECHANISM PREDICTION: solo competitive with E1 MLP 0.965935, disagreement 2.5-3.5 percent -- NOT the 10 percent E3 produced, which was weakness not diversity. GATE: blend must clear +0.0002 over champion 0.967451.

description: G1: FT-Transformer (rtdl) -- attention over feature tokens
te_cols: age daily_screen_time_hours social_media_hours gaming_hours work_study_hours sleep_hours notifications_per_day app_opens_per_day weekend_screen_time
notes: HYPOTHESIS: attention over feature tokens is a third inductive bias, distinct from both partitioning (trees) and a dense mixture (MLP) -- it models feature-to-feature interaction explicitly. This is the architecture axis the wall claim was never tested on: the -0.645 Spearman came from three tree libraries plus one MLP shape. MECHANISM PREDICTION: solo in the 0.964-0.967 band and disagreement 2.5-4 percent. The discriminating test is E3's lesson -- if solo collapses toward 0.94 the disagreement is weakness not diversity, and a high disagreement number alone must NOT be read as promise. GATE: blend must clear +0.0002 over champion 0.967451.

SHIP: subset selected by NESTED selection, not by hand. Ceiling scan of all 16,369 equal-weight subsets found a best of +0.000282, which alone is meaningless -- a max over thousands of candidates on the same OOF rows is the section 5 selection bias that gave S6E7 a fake +0.00014. So the SELECTION ITSELF was nested: each outer fold chose a subset using only the other four, then was scored on the fold the chooser never saw. Result: held-out +0.000282, 5/5 folds positive (+0.000195..+0.000374), and ALL FIVE FOLDS CHOSE THE IDENTICAL SUBSET from disjoint selection data -- so the nested and full-OOF numbers coincide and the procedure is deterministic under resampling, which selection bias cannot be. MECHANISM: every change from the champion swaps a weak leg for a strong one -- C4x (Optuna XGB, +0.000544 solo) added, B6 (weakest tree) dropped, E1 replaced by E2emb+F1real (the two stronger neural legs). This CORRECTS my earlier record of C4 as worth nothing: I tested one pairing (swap into the champion) and generalised from it. The lever was real; my test was too narrow.

description: G2: TabTransformer -- attention over categorical tokens only
te_cols: age daily_screen_time_hours social_media_hours gaming_hours work_study_hours sleep_hours notifications_per_day app_opens_per_day weekend_screen_time
notes: HYPOTHESIS: TabTransformer differs from FT-Transformer in a specific way -- it tokenises and attends over the CATEGORICAL columns only, concatenating the continuous block afterwards, whereas FT-Transformer tokenises every feature. With only 3 low-cardinality categoricals here and 18 continuous columns, that means most of our signal bypasses the attention entirely. MECHANISM PREDICTION: this should behave closer to a plain MLP than FT-Transformer does, so expect disagreement vs E1 BELOW FT-Transformer's, and solo in the 0.964-0.966 band. Run as the completing member of the architecture sweep rather than as a leg with a strong prior. CONFIG NOTE: batch 4096->1024 and d_token 64->32 after a CUDA OOM -- TabTransformer concatenates a much wider MLP head than FT-Transformer at the same token dim, so this is NOT a like-for-like capacity comparison with G1 and must not be read as one. GATE: blend must clear +0.0002 over champion 0.967451.

description: K_realmlp: GPU kernel (Tesla T4) on full data
te_cols: age daily_screen_time_hours social_media_hours gaming_hours work_study_hours sleep_hours notifications_per_day app_opens_per_day weekend_screen_time
notes: GPU KERNEL RUN requested to test these architectures on Kaggle hardware. description: logit stack over 16 legs, C=0.1
notes: B1 (Phase 2). HYPOTHESIS: every combiner this repo has ever shipped is an EQUAL-WEIGHT mean -- make_blend.py, subset_ceiling.py and nested_subset.py all search over WHICH legs, never HOW MUCH. An average can only ADD, so a leg that is weak but wrong in a useful direction can only dilute it. Both notebooks at the top of the public LB instead fit a logistic regression on the OOF matrix in LOGIT space and both report negative coefficients. MECHANISM PREDICTED, and confirmed on our own legs: (a) logits beat probabilities by ~10x (+0.000243 vs +0.000027) because this target saturates -- the top screen-time decile is ~100% positive, so near p=1 probabilities have no resolution left and log-odds still do; (b) a fitted combiner can SUBTRACT -- 4 of 16 weights are negative and K4node takes the third largest weight in the stack at -0.792, reversing this repo's conclusion that NODE is useless. That conclusion was a property of the COMBINER, not of the legs: the 65,519-subset equal-weight scan put NODE in exactly zero of its top 25 because an average has no way to use it. KNOWN OPTIMISM, stated before the result: the meta-model is refit inside each outer fold, but the base legs' OOF come from models fitted on this same partition, so a meta-model training on folds 1-4 consumes predictions from base models that saw fold 0. description: B3: fe_impute -- imputed columns ALONGSIDE the NaNs, on the B2 composition XGBoost

notes: B3 (Phase 2). HYPOTHESIS: every column is 4-20% missing and a ratio is NaN whenever EITHER operand is missing, so the composition family -- which just bought +0.001 on all three tree engines -- is unavailable on ~39% of rows, i.e. missing exactly where it would say the most. Model-imputing the nine numerics should restore that coverage. MECHANISM, and the reason the sign is not obvious: the public measurement of the SAME imputer runs both ways -- imputed values REPLACING the NaNs is negative, imputed values ALONGSIDE the retained NaN columns is +0.0012. A GBM's native NaN handling learns a default split DIRECTION per node, which is strictly more expressive than one imputed point estimate dragging the row toward the middle of its distribution; what the imputed copy adds is coverage for the derived features, not a better value for the raw one. So fe_impute AUGMENTS: it adds imp_* and impfe_* columns and the originals keep their NaNs, asserted in the notebook. LEAKAGE: the imputer predicts a FEATURE from other features and never sees y, so it is transductive unsupervised preprocessing, which section 2 licenses outside the CV loop. It is however the one family here that is not row-wise, so the row-wise purity assertion is scoped to exclude it and the imputed block gets its own assertions instead (observed values untouched, originals still carrying their NaNs). PRE-REGISTERED GATE: +0.0002 solo OOF over the B2 XGBoost composition leg f047412f = 0.968180, i.e. >= 0.968380. SECOND GATE, the one that decides shipping: a >= 0.0002 gain to the 21-leg stack over 0.969255. Context for reading a miss: TabM cleared its solo gate and still contributed only -0.000018 to the stack, so solo strength is no longer sufficient evidence for anything here.

L1lookupt is the only leg that ever broke this pack's correlation wall (max corr 0.9796 against a 0.9947 median) and it is also our strongest leg at 0.968626; it learns a d=128 embedding per exact observed value. num_as_cat is the tree-side version of the same representation: a many-vs-many categorical split instead of an ordered one. It acts on the central EDA finding that the value->target map is a lookup table (rates 0.119-0.986, Pearson(value, rate) = -0.044, only 47.8% of consecutive steps increasing). WHY RERUN IT: D2 scored 0.962343 and was rejected on solo strength, but it was run on the PRE-composition, PRE-Optuna base, and it was judged against subset_ceiling.py's rule that legs below 0.965 solo are 'strictly harmful' -- a rule that stack_logit.py has since shown is a property of the EQUAL-WEIGHT combiner and not of the legs (NODE, 0.9622 solo, takes the third-largest |weight| in the fitted stack). LightGBM parent chosen deliberately so the delta is attributable against D2, which used the same engine. FALSIFICATION: cardinalities run 18 to 1,459 levels over train union test with at most 22 test-only values; if the notebook's per-column level counts do not match those, the train-union-test vocabulary did not build and the run is void rather than negative. PRE-REGISTERED GATES, both written before the result is read. (1) solo OOF >= parent + 0.0002. (2) THE DECIDING GATE: >= +0.0002 to the honest 22-leg logit stack over 0.969314. A probe may clear (1) and miss (2) -- TabM and fe_impute both did exactly that, contributing +0.000027 and +0.000059 -- so solo strength is not sufficient evidence for shipping. STOP CONDITION: this round is the last regardless of outcome; a miss is not rescued by tuning C, changing the model seed, or hill-climbing over leg subsets.

description: P3: gate-2 stack contributions for N1/N2/N3 -- all three miss, zero submissions
notes: PHASE 3, gate 2 for the N-round -- the deciding gate, measured after the three probe rows 8f40573b (N1), ceb7f8c0 (N2) and ad5e827a (N3) were already logged with their pre-registered gates. All three MISS both gates. Contribution to the honest 22-leg logit stack over 0.969314: N1 fe_normalization -0.000000 (max corr 0.9977 vs B2xgb -- the HIGHEST correlation anywhere in the pack, above even the F1real/K1real rerun pair at 0.9975), N2 fe_interaction +0.000001 (max corr 0.9978), N3 num_as_cat +0.000029 (max corr 0.9783). All three admitted together: 0.969345, +0.000032. ZERO SUBMISSIONS -- 0a3c852e at LB 0.97056 stands. N1 MECHANISM: free_time = 24 - sleep - screen is structurally identical to the screen-time composition that cleared on all three engines at 5-6x the gate, and had MORE coverage to act on (80.9% vs 61.0%), yet produced a near-copy of its parent. Conclusion: the composition family did not work because it was a budget constraint, it worked because other_hours is a latent variable at solo AUC 0.765 that the trees could not otherwise reach. free_time has no such quantity behind it. Do not generalise 'budget constraints help' from B2. N2 MECHANISM: the family lost by 0.0003 pre-target-encoding and by 0.000018 now, on a base carrying TE, composition and Optuna params -- so it did not lose because the base could not use it. Settles the ambiguity in favour of the lookup reading: a ratio is a monotone transform and cannot represent a lookup table. N3 IS THE INFORMATIVE ONE and prices the section 6 wall as a QUANTITATIVE TRADE rather than a correlation across legs. It is the tree-side version of L1lookupt's representation (value as LABEL, not magnitude). Against orphan D2numcat, same representation on a much weaker base: D2numcat solo 0.962343, max corr 0.9717, stack +0.000030; N3 solo 0.966291, max corr 0.9783, stack +0.000029. +0.0040 of solo strength bought -0.000001 of stack contribution -- the leg got stronger and, by almost exactly enough to cancel it, less decorrelated. Moving ALONG the wall is free and worthless. L1lookupt did not move along it: it was simultaneously our strongest leg (0.968626) AND our most decorrelated (0.9796), which is why it was worth +0.0013 LB and why nothing since has repeated it. Vocabulary check passed (18/1397/729/401/601/451/231/166/1459 levels over train union test, all 39 test-only values present), so this is a negative and not a void run. STOP SIGNAL: seven consecutive probes now land inside +-0.00007 of the stack -- TabM +0.000027, fe_impute +0.000059, nonlinear meta -0.000042, orphan admission +0.000047, N1 -0.000000, N2 +0.000001, N3 +0.000029. Per playbook section 8 that is the stop condition, and a far sharper one than any single miss.

description: P3 negative: nonlinear and feature-gated meta-learners over the 22-leg pool
notes: PHASE 3 NEGATIVE, no artifacts -- a measurement, not a model. HYPOTHESIS: the 22-leg pack has median max-correlation 0.9947, so if the legs are near-duplicates GLOBALLY but differ in WHERE they are right, a combiner that switches on region would beat the fixed linear one. Tested three ways, all honest per-outer-fold refits at the frozen split, all against the shipped logistic stack at 0.969314 (C=0.1, LB 0.97056). RESULT: LightGBM meta (400 trees, 15 leaves, lr 0.03) over the 22 leg logits = 0.969272, -0.000042. The same plus the 9 raw numerics and a missing-count, i.e. feature-gated stacking = 0.969249, -0.000065. MECHANISM OF THE MISS, measured rather than assumed: the correlation between the tree-leg mean and the neural-leg mean is FLAT at 0.9785-0.9811 across all five missingness regimes and across composition-complete vs composition-broken rows, and the tree/neural/lookupT ordering barely moves. There is no heterogeneity for a gate to switch on. The legs differ in scale and sign, which a linear model already handles; they do not differ in region. CONCLUSION: the linear logit stack is the right combiner and the combiner axis is closed. Reproduce with scripts/leg_diversity.py sections 2-3.

description: P3 negative: admitting the 9 sub-0.965 orphan legs, all below the pool's median max-corr
notes: PHASE 3 NEGATIVE, no artifacts -- a measurement, not a model. HYPOTHESIS: nine Phase 1 legs sit on disk with complete oof+test artifacts on the frozen partition, excluded by subset_ceiling.py's rule that legs below 0.965 solo are 'strictly harmful'. That rule was measured under an EQUAL-WEIGHT MEAN, where a weak leg can only dilute, and stack_logit.py has since shown it is a property of the combiner and not of the legs -- K4node at 0.9622 solo takes the third-largest |weight| in the fitted stack. Every one of the nine sits BELOW the pool's 0.9947 median max-correlation. Admitting them costs zero compute and zero submissions, so the only question was whether they help. PRE-REGISTERED GATE: +0.0002 to the honest 22-leg logit stack over 0.969314. RESULT: all nine together = 0.969361, +0.000047 -- a quarter of the gate. Dropping the seed twin changes nothing (0.969363). Add-one: D2numcat +0.000030 (largest), D2blookup +0.000015, E3raw +0.000008, A2es400 +0.000001, and v1anchor / A1seed / B1inter / G2tabtf / K3tabtf all -0.000001. THE FINDING, and the reason this row exists: K3tabtf has max corr 0.9251 against a pool whose median is 0.9947 -- by a wide margin the most decorrelated leg we own -- and it contributes -0.000001, because 0.015 AUC below the pack is noise however uncorrelated that noise is. MAX-CORRELATION DOES NOT PREDICT STACK CONTRIBUTION. L1lookupt paid (+0.0013 LB) because it was simultaneously our STRONGEST leg at 0.968626 AND decorrelated; decorrelation is a multiplier on strength, not a substitute for it. PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE: 'it will be different' is not a hypothesis and must not justify a future probe. SEED COROLLARY, priced rather than argued: A1seed, the one seed-only twin we own, contributes -0.000001, matching the public library's seed-averaged member at +0.000000 -- the standing instruction not to spend on seed variants is correct on our own data. Reproduce with scripts/leg_diversity.py sections 1 and 4.

description: R1: ModernNCA retrieval head on L1lookupt's per-value representation
notes: R1 ModernNCA -- RETRIEVAL over the lookup representation. First probe after the Phase 3 stop signal, run because it has a MECHANISM rather than 'it will be different', which the orphan measurement (commit 816087a) established is not a sufficient justification. HYPOTHESIS: ModernNCA (Ye et al., ICLR 2025) predicts a row by soft k-NN over the training set in a learned metric space -- p(y=1|q) = sum_j softmax(-||f(q)-f(x_j)||_2) * y_j. This repo's central EDA finding is that the value->target map is a LOOKUP TABLE (rates 0.119-0.986, Pearson(value, rate) = -0.044, only 47.8% of consecutive steps increasing), and retrieval IS lookup. The only leg that ever broke the section 6 wall, L1lookupt, won by treating the value as a LABEL rather than a magnitude (solo 0.968626, max corr 0.9796 against a 0.9947 median, worth +0.0013 LB), and nothing since has repeated it. WHY THE INPUT REPRESENTATION IS THE WHOLE EXPERIMENT: a soft-kNN in a learned CONTINUOUS metric places near VALUES near each other, which is exactly the wrong geometry for a non-monotone lattice -- the same reason B1/N2's ratios failed, a monotone transform cannot represent a lookup. So this is run on the per-value embedding, not on rank-gauss scalars. The prediction for the scalar version, pre-registered here so it cannot be claimed later: solo ~0.966, max corr > 0.995, contribution ~0, i.e. our eighth neural shape and not worth the GPU hour. M1 TabM is the precedent -- fed the TREE representation a packed MLP ensemble re-derived the tree solution (nearest neighbours 0.9847-0.9867 with the trees, solo equal to C4x's to four decimals). The representation decides what a model becomes. STRICT TWIN: the ONLY CFG field that differs from L1lookupt (dada9e2d) is `learner`, checked by run_local.py --diff-vs. At the code level the mnca branch is spliced INTO the lookupt branch and shares the vocabulary, rank-gauss and PLR code verbatim -- verified as the original 119 lines reindented by exactly 4 spaces -- so the two cannot drift apart and the delta is attributable to the HEAD (retrieval vs transformer) over an identical input. It is not a single-parameter ablation: the encoder is shallow (ModernNCA's own finding is that the retrieval does the work) and the loss is the NCA log-likelihood, not BCE. Say that plainly rather than overclaiming the twin. PRE-REGISTERED GATES, both written before the result is read. (1) solo OOF >= 0.9655 -- the same bar L1lookupt was held to, i.e. the bar for 'a leg that could matter'; K3tabtf proved a weak leg contributes nothing however decorrelated (max corr 0.9251, contribution -0.000001). (2) THE DECIDING GATE: >= +0.0002 to the honest 22-leg logit stack over 0.969314. Seven consecutive probes have missed gate 2 while two of them cleared gate 1, so gate 1 is not evidence for shipping. FALSIFICATION, pre-registered so the outcome is readable either way. (a) Strong but max corr >= 0.995 against L1lookupt = retrieval re-derived the transformer's solution from the shared representation; the head does not matter, the representation does -- the TabM outcome. (b) Decorrelated (< 0.99) but solo < 0.960 = the other jaw of the wall, decorrelated-but-weak, the K3tabtf outcome. (c) Only simultaneously strong AND decorrelated refutes the wall, which is what L1lookupt did and what would make this worth a submission. HONEST PRIOR: I expect (a) or a miss -- solo 0.966-0.969, corr 0.97-0.98 with L1lookupt, contribution +0.0000 to +0.0001. Clearing gate 2 would be a genuine surprise. IMPLEMENTATION NOTES that bear on reading the number: candidates are resampled every step (16,384 of ~553k, ~3%) which is ModernNCA's scalability trick; SELF-RETRIEVAL IS MASKED, since a row reading its own label is the NCA form of a target leak; per-epoch early stopping uses a fixed 65,536-candidate bank for speed, but the FINAL oof/test artifacts retrieve over the ENTIRE training fold, which is ModernNCA as published. Distances are Euclidean, not squared, per the paper -- squaring collapses the neighbourhood towards a hard 1-NN. The streaming log-sum-exp that replaces the 300 GB dense score matrix was verified against the dense computation to 4e-7 at five chunk sizes including 1, plus the all-masked-block and self-exclusion edge cases. STOP CONDITION: one run. A miss is not rescued by tuning the candidate count, the metric dimension, the model seed, or C in the stack.

description: P4: R1 mnca gate 2 -- strongest AND most decorrelated leg we own, and it MISSES
notes: PHASE 4 gate 2 for R1 (9107a864), plus the decomposition that explains it. No artifacts -- a measurement. RESULT: R1 mnca is our STRONGEST leg (solo 0.968722 vs L1lookupt 0.968626), it takes the LARGEST |weight| of all 23 legs in the fitted stack, its max corr against the pool is 0.9771 against a pool median of 0.9947 -- MORE decorrelated than L1lookupt's 0.9796 -- and it correlates only 0.9689 with L1lookupt, so it is NOT a copy of it. That is simultaneously strongest AND most decorrelated: outcome (c) of the pre-registered falsification, the quadrant section 6 says is empty, and the SECOND counter-example to the wall after L1lookupt. AND IT STILL MISSES: contribution +0.000120 against a +0.0002 gate. 23-leg stack 0.969434 vs the shipped 22-leg 0.969314. My own pre-registered prediction was outcome (a) -- strong but corr >= 0.995, a re-derivation of L1lookupt -- and that was WRONG; it is genuinely a different model. The gate call was right for the wrong reason, so record the reason. THE MECHANISM, measured not assumed. Removing L1lookupt from the pool and adding each leg back alone: 21 legs (neither) 0.968793; +L1lookupt 0.969314 (+0.000520); +mnca INSTEAD 0.969323 (+0.000530); +BOTH 0.969434 (+0.000641). Either lookup leg alone is worth ~+0.00052 to the stack. Together they are worth +0.000641, not +0.001050 -- 64% of their value is the SAME value. The marginal is near-symmetric (mnca given L1 +0.000120, L1 given mnca +0.000111), so this is not 'mnca is redundant', it is 'the SECOND lookup leg is redundant, whichever one it is'. CONCLUSION, and the generalisation of the TabM lesson: THE REPRESENTATION IS THE UNIT OF ENSEMBLE VALUE, NOT THE MODEL. A 4-layer transformer with attention over feature tokens and a soft-kNN metric learner share no inductive bias whatsoever, yet reading the same per-value lookup representation they deliver the same +0.00052 and 64% of it is the same +0.00052. What L1lookupt bought was never 'a transformer'; it was ACCESS to the lookup representation, and that access is now saturated. A third architecture on the same representation is predicted to buy ~+0.0001 and must not be run on the strength of this row. CORRELATION STRUCTURE IS NOT VALUE STRUCTURE, from the opposite direction to the Phase 3 finding: the two legs correlate only 0.9689 and still share 64% of their contribution. Their correlation PROFILES are also very different -- mnca is closer to the trees (B2blgb 0.9771 vs L1's 0.9633, B2xgb 0.9749 vs 0.9688) and much further from the neural legs (F1real 0.8628 vs L1's 0.9305, K4node 0.9062 vs 0.9536), i.e. retrieval reads the lookup lattice the way a tree does while the transformer reads it the way a net does. Different neighbours, same value. DECISION: gate 2 missed, so nothing ships on this probe's own terms and the mnca leg is NOT submitted as a gate clearance. Whether to submit the 23-leg stack at all is a SEPARATE question on the 0a3c852e precedent (submit the OOF champion so it exists as a selectable entry at the 2026-08-31 deadline, not to learn anything): predicted LB 0.969434 + 0.00128 = 0.97071 against the standing 0.97056, i.e. +0.00015 against a leaderboard resolution of 0.00014 -- a number we could barely read. That is a finals-selection call, not a probe result. NOT RUN, and the one open question: mnca on rank-gauss SCALARS instead of the per-value embedding, which would attribute this to the representation directly. Pre-registered prediction from before R1 ran, unchanged: solo ~0.966, max corr > 0.995, contribution ~0. The overlap decomposition above already answers the question it was designed to answer, which is why it was not run. Reproduce all of this with scripts/leg_probe.py 9107a864.

description: logit stack over 23 legs, C=0.1
notes:
FINALS SELECTION, NOT A GATE CLEARANCE. 23-leg logit stack = the shipped 22 (0a3c852e, LB 0.97056) plus R1mnca (9107a864). R1mnca MISSED gate 2 -- contribution +0.000120 against the +0.0002 gate -- and nothing ships on a miss. This submission is on the 0a3c852e precedent instead: submit the OOF champion so it EXISTS as a selectable entry at the 2026-08-31 deadline, not to learn anything. User decision, taken with the +0.00015 expected delta stated up front.
PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTION, written before the score is read. OOF 0.969434 + the measured CV->LB stack offset 0.00128 (+/- 0.000029 over three consecutive stack submissions: 16-leg, 19-leg, 22-leg) = LB 0.97071. Standing best 0.97056. Expected delta +0.00015 against a leaderboard resolution of 0.00014 -- a number we can barely read, which is the honest reason this is a selection call and not evidence.
HOW TO READ THE RESULT. (a) 0.97069-0.97074: the offset holds a FOURTH time and the 23-leg stack becomes Final A on OOF, which is the selection rule this repo has used throughout. (b) <= 0.97056: the +0.000120 OOF gain did not transfer, which is exactly what a sub-resolution gain looks like and is CONSISTENT with the gate-2 miss rather than a contradiction of it; keep the 22-leg stack as Final A. (c) > 0.9708: the offset itself moved, which would be new information about the meta-fit optimism and would need explaining before any of it is trusted.
DO NOT RESCUE A DISAPPOINTING NUMBER. No re-fit at another C, no re-submission at another member set, no hill-climb over legs on the strength of this row. Four consecutive probes have landed inside +/- 0.00007 and section 5 already warns that a hill-climb at this scale is noise.
Members: the 22 of subset_ceiling.LEGS + 9107a864. Reproduce: python scripts/stack_logit.py --runs $(python -c "from subset_ceiling import LEGS; print(*LEGS.values())") 9107a864 ||| RESULT, read after the pre-registration above was written. LB 0.97060 against a predicted 0.97071. That is outcome (b) and a MISS on the prediction: +0.000040 over the standing 0.97056, not the +0.000150 predicted, i.e. only 33% of the +0.000120 OOF gain transferred. The 23-leg stack is now BOTH the OOF champion (0.969434) and the LB champion (0.97060), so it becomes Final A with no conflict between the two selection criteria -- but it wins the LB by 0.00004 against a resolution of 0.00014, which is to say it does not measurably win at all. Treat the 22- and 23-leg stacks as tied. THE REAL FINDING IS THE OFFSET, AND IT IS NOT A CONSTANT. Across all four stack submissions the CV->LB offset DECAYS MONOTONICALLY with pool size: 16 legs 0.001304, 19 legs 0.001282, 22 legs 0.001246, 23 legs 0.001166. The first three were read as a constant 0.001277 +/- 0.000029 and that reading was WRONG -- it was three points on a slope, and the fourth point falls 3.8 sigma below the mean of the first three. Offset = LB - OOF, so a FALLING offset means the OOF is becoming progressively more OPTIMISTIC as legs are added. That is exactly what a fitted meta-model does: more members, more parameters, more fit to the noise in the OOF matrix, and honest_oof's per-outer-fold refit does not remove it because every leg's OOF was itself produced on this same partition. TRANSFER RATIO, the operational form of the same number: 16->19 legs OOF +0.001252 / LB +0.001230 = 98% transferred; 19->22 OOF +0.000086 / LB +0.000050 = 58%; 22->23 OOF +0.000120 / LB +0.000040 = 33%. The one large genuine gain transferred essentially in full; the marginal gains transfer progressively less. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE GATE, and this is the part that changes future decisions. The +0.0002 gate is stated in OOF units and has been read throughout as if OOF units were LB units. At the current pool size a leg that exactly clears it is worth roughly +0.00007 on the leaderboard -- HALF the leaderboard's own resolution. The gate has been silently deflating in value as the pool grew. It is not that the gate was set too low; it is that OOF and LB are no longer the same currency at 23 legs. Any future leg should be judged on OOF contribution x the current transfer ratio, and on that arithmetic no single additional leg of the kind we know how to build can move this leaderboard. This also RETROSPECTIVELY VINDICATES the gate-2 miss on R1mnca: the gate said the leg was not worth shipping on its own terms, the LB agreed to within a number too small to read, and the submission was correctly framed as finals selection rather than as evidence.

description: P5: TabICLv2 feasibility -- subsetting is not the obstacle, the representation is
notes: PHASE 5 feasibility probe, TABULAR FOUNDATION MODELS. Exploratory measurement, NOT a gated leg probe -- no gate was pre-registered because nothing was going to be submitted from it; the decision it feeds is whether to spend Kaggle GPU hours on a TFM leg at all. No artifacts. Reproduce with scripts/tfm_probe.py. THE PREMISE THAT BLOCKED THIS HAS EXPIRED. The repo never tried a TFM because TabPFN v2 capped at ~10k rows against our 691,369. The released models moved: TabPFN-3 states 1,000,000 x 200 and TabICLv2 states 500K with CPU/disk offload. Our table fits inside both, so subsetting is not even required -- and for an in-context learner 'train on a subset and extend to the whole dataset' is not a workaround in the first place, since the training set IS the context and context-ensembling is free. TabICLv2 chosen over TabPFN-3 for a NON-TECHNICAL reason worth recording: TabICL is BSD-3 (soda-inria/Inria), while the TabPFN-3 weights carry a licence forbidding commercial and production use. A no-prize Playground competition is very probably fine under it, but 'very probably fine' is not a licence review and the BSD option cost nothing. tabicl 2.1.1, checkpoint tabicl-classifier-v2-20260212, installed with zero dependency upgrades. MEASURED on fold 0 of the frozen partition, 20,000 query rows, RTX 3060 laptop, ~15 min total, ZERO Kaggle GPU hours and ZERO submissions spent. AUC standard error at n=20k is about +/-0.002, so these are NOT comparable to runs.csv OOF at the fourth decimal -- but every gap that matters below is ten times that. ARM A, single context, raw features, growing: 4k 0.933739 | 8k 0.936880 | 16k 0.938499 | 32k 0.939397 | 69k 0.940215. The curve is FLAT by 32k -- the last doubling buys +0.0008. ARM B, the actual proposal: 8 DISJOINT stratified contexts partitioning the training fold, 16k each, 128k rows seen in total, averaged in LOGIT space. Result 0.939787, and it does NOT beat a single 69k context (0.940215) despite seeing nearly twice the rows. Solo blocks were 0.9377-0.9384 and the ensemble converged by block 4. So context-ensembling works, is cheap, and buys nothing here: both routes plateau at ~0.940, which is our WORST LEG EVER (E3raw 0.9405) and 0.022 below the pool floor. ARM C, and this is the finding: SAME model, SAME 16k context, changing ONLY the representation from raw values to the target-encoded lookup rate -> 0.958762. +0.019 from the representation against +0.007 from a 17x larger context. And 0.958762 is an UPPER BOUND, because the context rows see their own labels through the TE (fit on the 553k training fold, smoothed at 50); the query rows are clean, so the comparison is honest in the direction that matters. MECHANISM. This data is a value->target LOOKUP TABLE -- rates 0.119-0.986, Pearson(value, rate) = -0.044, only 47.8% of consecutive steps increasing, cardinality to 1,459. A TFM normalises an integer code and reads it as a MAGNITUDE, so it cannot see a non-monotonic lookup table no matter how much context it is given. That is why arm A saturates 0.028 below our best leg while arm C recovers two thirds of the gap by changing one thing. CONCLUSION: DO NOT BUILD A TFM LEG. The ceiling is representational, not one of dataset size, context size, or GPU budget -- which is PHASE 4's finding ('the representation is the unit of ensemble value') arriving from a third independent direction, and the first time it has been demonstrated on a model family trained by somebody else on data that is not ours. Even the optimistic arm C enters at ~0.958 against a pool floor of 0.9622, and PHASE 3 measured that a leg weaker than the pool contributes nothing however decorrelated (K3tabtf: max corr 0.9251 against a 0.9947 median, contribution -0.000001). Compose that with PHASE 5's transfer ratio -- 33% of OOF gain reaching the LB at 23 legs -- and the expected leaderboard value of a TFM leg is indistinguishable from zero. WHAT WOULD CHANGE THIS ANSWER: a TFM whose preprocessing treats high-cardinality integer columns as CATEGORICAL rather than numeric, which would let arm A read the lookup table directly. If one ships before 2026-08-31, arm A is the two-line rerun that tests it. COST OF THE ANSWER: ~15 minutes local GPU and a 250kB pip install, versus the multi-hour Kaggle GPU leg it replaced. Cheap negatives before expensive positives -- playbook section 8.
